# Database — MySQL schema and MongoDB migration

* **Engine:** MySQL 8.0+ · InnoDB · `utf8mb4_unicode_ci`
* **Access layer:** Prisma ORM 6.19 (`server/prisma/schema.prisma`)
* **Migrations:** `server/prisma/migrations/` (version-controlled SQL generated by Prisma Migrate)
* **Identifiers:** `INT AUTO_INCREMENT` primary keys throughout. They are consistent, JSON-safe, and far beyond a college's scale.

## Entity overview

```
departments 1─* courses 1─* sections 1─* students *─1 users
     │              │            │            │
     └──* staff *─1 users        │            ├──* attendance_records *─1 class_sessions *─1 sections/subjects
                    │            │            └──* student_fee_records *─1 fee_structures *─0..1 courses
                    └──* staff_assignments *─1 subjects *─1 courses       │
                                   *─1 sections                           └──* payments
study_materials *─1 subjects, *─0..1 sections, *─1 users (uploader)
notifications 1─* notification_recipients *─1 users
announcements *─0..1 users (author)
teacher_alerts *─1 sections, *─1 staff, *─0..1 subjects, *─1 users (raised by)
audit_logs *─0..1 users (actor)
```

## Tables

| Table | Purpose | Key constraints |
|---|---|---|
| `users` | Shared identity for every account: username, email, bcrypt hash, role (`STUDENT`/`STAFF`/`ADMIN`), status (`PENDING`/`ACTIVE`/`INACTIVE`), `token_version` | UNIQUE `username`, UNIQUE `email`, INDEX (`role`,`status`) |
| `students` | Student profile: roll number, section, admission year, representative designation (`NONE`/`CR`/`LR`) | UNIQUE `user_id`, UNIQUE `roll_number`, FK section RESTRICT |
| `staff` | Staff profile: employee ID, department, designation | UNIQUE `user_id`, UNIQUE `employee_id` |
| `departments` | Academic departments | UNIQUE `code` |
| `courses` | Programmes (e.g. CSE — B.Tech Computer Science & Engineering) | UNIQUE `code`, FK department |
| `sections` | Class groups (course + year of study + name, e.g. CSE 3-A) | UNIQUE (`course_id`,`year_of_study`,`name`) |
| `subjects` | Subjects taught to a course/year | UNIQUE `code`, INDEX (`course_id`,`year_of_study`) |
| `staff_assignments` | Who teaches which subject to which section. This is the source of staff permissions | UNIQUE (`staff_id`,`subject_id`,`section_id`) |
| `class_sessions` | One taught period | UNIQUE (`section_id`,`date`,`period`), INDEX (`subject_id`,`date`), (`staff_id`,`date`) |
| `attendance_records` | One student's status in a session (`PRESENT`/`ABSENT`/`LATE`) | UNIQUE (`session_id`,`student_id`), CASCADE on session delete |
| `fee_structures` | Fee templates (name, academic year, optional course/year, amount, due date) | `amount DECIMAL(10,2)` |
| `student_fee_records` | A fee billed to a student: amount, concession, amount paid, status, due date | UNIQUE (`student_id`,`fee_structure_id`), INDEX (`status`,`due_date`) |
| `payments` | Receipts recorded by the accounts office; `RECORDED` or `VOIDED` (never edited) | UNIQUE `receipt_no`, FK fee record RESTRICT |
| `study_materials` | File metadata: title, unit, subject, optional section, stored and original names, MIME type, size, download count, uploader | UNIQUE `stored_name` |
| `notifications` | A message plus its audience description | INDEX (`sender_id`,`created_at`) |
| `notification_recipients` | Per-user delivery with `read_at` | UNIQUE (`notification_id`,`user_id`), INDEX (`user_id`,`read_at`) |
| `announcements` | Notice-board entries (audience, pinned, expiry) | INDEX (`audience`,`published_at`) |
| `teacher_alerts` | CR/LR alerts: section, teacher, period, status (`OPEN`/`ACKNOWLEDGED`/`RESOLVED`), response | INDEX (`staff_id`,`status`) |
| `audit_logs` | Who did what and when, with JSON metadata and IP address | INDEX `created_at`, (`actor_id`,`created_at`), (`entity_type`,`entity_id`) |

**Design choices**
* **No `roles` table.** Roles are a controlled `ENUM`, and CR/LR are designations on `students`. Administrators are only ever created by another administrator or the CLI.
* **No `student_enrollments` table.** A student belongs to exactly one section, and a section's subjects come from `staff_assignments`. A separate enrolment table would duplicate that information.
* **Money uses `DECIMAL(10,2)`**, never floats. Payment recording and voiding run in transactions with optimistic concurrency on `amount_paid`.
* **Referential actions.** `RESTRICT` protects academic and financial history. `CASCADE` is used only for owned children (a session's attendance records, a notification's recipients). `SET NULL` is used for optional authorship (audit actor, notification sender).

## Initialising and evolving the schema

| Situation | Command | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh database (any environment) | `npm run db:deploy` | Creates the database if your user may, and applies all migrations |
| Changing the schema (development) | edit `schema.prisma`, then `npm run db:migrate -- --name <change>` | Generates a new SQL migration and applies it |
| Production / CI | `npm run db:deploy` | Applies pending migrations only — never resets data |
| Start over (development only) | `npm run db:reset` | **Drops all data**, then re-applies migrations |
| Demo data (development only) | `npm run db:seed` | Refuses if any account exists or `NODE_ENV=production` |

Verified on 2026-10-13: `migrate deploy` built the complete schema (20 tables including `_prisma_migrations`, 37 foreign keys) on an empty MySQL 8.0.43 server, and `prisma migrate diff` reports no drift between the migrations and the live development database.

## MongoDB → MySQL migration

### What the original project stored
| Original | Persistence | Migrated to |
|---|---|---|
| `Student` (Mongoose): fullName, rollNumber, username, **plaintext** password, email, mobile, course (text), section (text), role (self-chosen) | MongoDB | `users` + `students` (+ `courses`/`sections`) |
| `Teacher` (Mongoose): teacherName, teacherId, username, plaintext password, email, mobile, department (text) | MongoDB (never used by any route) | `users` + `staff` (+ `departments`) |
| `Material` (Mongoose): subject, unit, course, section, teacher, **file name string** | MongoDB | `study_materials` (files must be re-uploaded — see below) |
| Attendance, fees, notifications, teacher alerts | **In-memory arrays** (lost on every restart) | `class_sessions`/`attendance_records`, `fee_structures`/`student_fee_records`/`payments`, `notifications`/`notification_recipients`, `teacher_alerts` |
| `models/Attendance.js`, `Fees.js`, `Notification.js` | Empty files | — |

### Data found on this machine
The local MongoDB server (127.0.0.1:27017) was inspected on 2026-10-13. **No `studentexpressoo` database exists**, so there was no production data to migrate. The new database was initialised from the migrations, and development demo data is loaded separately with `npm run db:seed`.

### Importing data from the original MongoDB version
If the original app was used on another machine, its data can be imported with the provided script. The MongoDB driver isn't needed: the script reads standard `mongoexport` JSON.

```bash
# 1. On the machine with the old data
mongoexport --db studentexpressoo --collection students  --jsonArray --out students.json
mongoexport --db studentexpressoo --collection teachers  --jsonArray --out teachers.json
mongoexport --db studentexpressoo --collection materials --jsonArray --out materials.json

# 2. Preview (writes nothing, produces import-report.dry-run.json)
npm run import-mongo -- --dir ./mongo-export --dry-run

# 3. Import (produces import-report.json with an ObjectId → MySQL id map)
npm run import-mongo -- --dir ./mongo-export
```

Mapping rules (implemented in `server/scripts/import-mongo-export.js`):
* **ObjectIds** become new `INT` ids. The report records `mongoId → { userId, studentId }` for traceability.
* **Plaintext passwords** are bcrypt-hashed, so users keep their existing password.
* **Free-text course/section values** become `courses`/`sections` rows (codes are normalised, e.g. `cse` → `CSE`). The year of study is unknown in the old data and defaults to 1; these sections are listed under `needsReview`.
* **Roles chosen at public sign-up are not trusted.** `CR`/`LR` become representative designations. `Teacher` becomes a **PENDING** staff account awaiting approval. `Admin` is **skipped** (create admins with `npm run create-admin`).
* **Teachers** are imported as PENDING staff for administrator approval.
* **Existing users** (matching username, email, roll number or employee ID) are skipped, never overwritten, so the import is safe to re-run.
* **Materials cannot be migrated.** The old app stored only a file name, never the file. Each one is listed under `notMigrated` so teachers can re-upload it.
* An `audit_logs` entry records the import.

Verification performed on 2026-10-13 against the test database with a synthetic export shaped like the original Mongoose documents:
* The dry run planned 2 students and 2 staff, with 1 skip (the self-registered "Admin").
* The import created them, with the CR designation preserved and old passwords still valid as bcrypt hashes.
* A re-run imported 0 and skipped 5.

### Removal of MongoDB
* `mongoose` and `mongodb` are no longer dependencies anywhere in the workspace (`npm ls mongoose mongodb` → empty).
* There is no MongoDB connection string or model in the source tree, and the API starts with MySQL only.
* The original MongoDB implementation is preserved, unchanged, in `../_backup/StudentExpressoo-original-mongodb-2026-10-13.tar.gz` (outside the project folder).

## Backups
For production, schedule `mysqldump --single-transaction --routines student_expressoo` (or your managed provider's snapshots) **and** back up `server/uploads/`. Material metadata is in MySQL, but the files themselves live on disk.
